newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Yachting-Missing French yachtsman climbs on life raft.
newsitem.headline: Yachting-Missing French yachtsman climbs on life raft.

text.p: Australian rescue officials said on Monday French yachtsman Thierry Dubois had climbed on to a life raft dropped by an Australian air force plane in the Southern Ocean.
But there was no sign yet of Britain's Tony Bullimore, another round-the-world solo yachtsman who had set off distress signals on Sunday night.
Australian Defence Force spokesman Colonel Andrew Reynolds told Reuters two planes had been involved in finding Dubois. Rafts dropped by the first plane had proved ineffective.

The first raft Dubois had climbed aboard capsized but he then managed to climb aboard another raft dropped by the second rescue plane about 6 p.m. local time (1000 GMT), about 1,400 nautical miles southwest of Perth.
Bullimore, 56, on board Global Exide Challenger, and 29-year-old Dubois on board Amnesty International sent out distress calls late on Sunday after sailing into a storm.

The two competitors in the Vendee Globe round-the-world race hit difficulties about 120 nautical miles south of the region where French yachtsman Raphael Dinelli was rescued from his sinking yacht two days after Christmas.
